title: Region failover sequencing bug and priority shed policy consolidation
creator: Anita Choudhary
description: Summary: On 2026-03-01 at ~08:03 UTC a multi-region failover sequence caused a correlated set of circuit-breaker (CB) openings and priority queue shedding across EU and US regions, resulting in a 28-minute continuous SLO violation for the generation latency P99 for several high-throughput customers. The orchestrator replayed an out-of-order failover sequence after a partial control-plane partition which briefly allowed dual warmup eviction and simultaneous CB signals. This ticket captures the incident analysis, immediate mitigations, and cross-team corrective plan to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: SLO: generation P99 latency exceeded target (1.2s -> observed 3.8s) for 28 minutes
Affected regions: EU-west-1 primary, US-east-1 secondary (sticky affinity misrouted to secondary under failover)
Customers: 7 high-throughput tenants experienced increased 429/503 errors and tail latency spikes
Operational: automated rollback to lower model concurrency triggered but did not fully alleviate due to inter-region backpressure
timeline: 2026-03-01 08:02:38 UTC - Control plane observed degraded heartbeat from EU controller (brief partition).
2026-03-01 08:03:12 UTC - Failover sequencer initiated recovery path; an out-of-order step replay occurred due to a race with cached state.
2026-03-01 08:03:45 UTC - Multiple region-level CBs transitioned to OPEN concurrently; priority shed started in US region.
2026-03-01 08:05:20 UTC - Symptoms: elevated queue length, KV-cache warmup failures, and increased tail latencies reported by dashboards.
2026-03-01 08:20:00 UTC - On-call performed manual mitigation: paused cross-region failovers and forced a controlled warmup for EU hot keys.
2026-03-01 08:30:00 UTC - Traffic gradually recovered; automated rollback reduced concurrency which helped but did not fully restore P99 until 08:35 UTC.
root_cause: A race condition in the failover sequencer allowed a replay of a previously-applied step (evict->warmup) without acquiring the global failover lock. This produced temporary state divergence between EU and US orchestrators. Divergent state caused near-simultaneous CB open signals and an overly aggressive priority shed in the secondary region. Secondary causes: insufficient hysteresis on per-region CB propagation and lack of a guarded decoupling layer between CB open events and global priority-shed policy evaluation.
remediation_actions: Short-term mitigation: introduce a temporary mutex in the sequencer to serialize failover steps across regions (owner: SRE - Luis Fernandez, ETA: 2d, status: done),
Rollback safeguard: pin model concurrency lower for affected tenants during cross-region failover windows until controls land (owner: Customer Success - Maya Patel, ETA: 1d, status: done),
Hotfix: increase CB propagation backoff to add 10s hysteresis for inter-region broadcasts (owner: Runtime - Omar Shah, ETA: 3d, status: in progress),
Observability: add synthetic canary key traffic and dedicated CB transition traces to surface sequential misordering (owner: Observability - Priya Gupta, ETA: 5d, status: in progress)
followup_tasks: Design and implement sequencer global lockless protocol (goal: eliminate replay risk without global mutex) - RFC due 2026-03-12 (owner: Runtime - Marco Li, estimate: 8),
Consolidate priority-shed policy evaluation into a single policy engine that uses idempotent CB signals and tenant-scoped hysteresis (owner: Platform - Ingrid Sørensen, estimate: 5),
Extend chaos test suite to simulate staggered control-plane partitions and CB race conditions (owner: Reliability - Daniel Kim, estimate: 5),
Run a cross-region canary for 72h after fixes with success criteria: no P99 regression >10% vs baseline and no simultaneous CB OPEN across regions for same tenant (owner: SRE, estimate: 3),
Customer communications: post-incident summary and mitigation steps to the 7 affected tenants with timeline and credits offer (owner: CS - Maya Patel, due: 2026-03-06)
metrics_observed: CB open rate (per-region): EU 3x baseline during incident window, US 2.7x
priority-shed invocations: 14K requests dropped in US region over 28 minutes
queue depth: 4x typical for hot-shard affinity queues
monitoring_changes: Add trace ID tagging for failover sequencer runs to correlate with CB state transitions (owner: Observability - Priya Gupta).
New alert: CB_CONCURRENT_OPEN_COUNT > 1 for same-tenant across regions for >10s -> P0 paging (owner: SRE).
Dashboard: cross-region CB heatmap with tenant filter (owner: Platform).
decision_log: 2026-03-01 09:10 UTC - Agreed to deploy temporary sequencer mutex to stop immediate replay risk (vote: unanimous).
2026-03-02 14:30 UTC - Decided to prioritize policy consolidation over incremental heuristics to avoid repeat maintenance burden (owners assigned).
2026-03-04 11:00 UTC - Customer credit offer approved for 7 tenants impacted (value capped per SLA).
notes: Trade-offs considered: global mutex vs lockless protocol. We implemented a short-term mutex to reduce blast radius quickly; longer-term work will target lockless guarantees to avoid throughput cliffs.
Testing notes: replay of sequencing race was reproducible in stage with controlled partition delay of 250-700ms; failure mode depends on interleaved cache eviction ack ordering.
Related: this incident reuses learnings from ENG-35890 (kv-cache warmup starvation) and should be coordinated with that roadmap.
